To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the pass through from the exchange rate to the price level in Ireland is higher than that in other small open economies.

(i) the pass through of exchange rates to consumer prices in the 1993-2002 period is consistent with a model where the UK price level is the equilibrium price level in Ireland; (ii) the rate of pass-through is lower in the 1997-2002 period than in the 1994-1997 period.

the rate of pass-through of exchange rate changes into Irish inflation has been lower in recent years than in the 1992-96 period, the speed of adjustment is lower in recent years, and that the speed of adjustment has been affected by the ERM crisis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of expectations of the exchange rate and the price level in determining the rate of pass-through of exchange rate changes into Irish inflation.
the transmission of external shocks into the Irish economy.
the role played by the exchange rate in the transmission of inflationary pressures from abroad to Ireland.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

there is a strong link between Irish and UK inflation, and that the pass-through of external shocks into domestic inflation has increased since the ERM crisis, but has remained at a relatively high level since then.
the pass through of the euro exchange rate to Irish consumer prices will be lower in the future than it was during the period of the Irish pound.
the Irish consumer price index is a good indicator of the underlying inflationary trend in the Irish economy and that the pass-through of exchange rate changes is not complete.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Irish rate of pass through to exchange rates has declined in the 1999s.

, as the Irish economy has become more open to international competition and as the exchange rate regime has become more flexible, the pass-through of exchange rate changes into Irish consumer prices has increased.
the ERM crisis had a lasting effect on the speed of adjustment in Irish inflation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Irish economy has become increasingly integrated with the UK economy.
exchange rates are an important determinant of Irish inflation.
, in the short run, the pass through of exchange rates into Irish inflation is not as strong as the literature has suggested.
